beliefs.title: AI security overlaps, not replaces
beliefs.body: I see AI security and cybersecurity as overlapping fields, like a Venn diagram, not one subsuming the other. AI's probabilistic nature and growing autonomy still deserve tailored defences even where existing controls help.

beliefs.title: Data attacks start early
beliefs.body: The biggest risks to data are poisoning training data and manipulating features or datasets, and they show up at the earliest stages of an attack, not at the model. If training data is not validated, everything downstream inherits the problem.

beliefs.title: Supply chain is the whole pipeline
beliefs.body: A model file, a third-party library, a CI/CD pipeline, a cloud provider: any one of these can be the entry point, so I treat supply chain risk as running through the entire life cycle, not just the dependencies list.

beliefs.title: Structure follows headcount, not fashion
beliefs.body: Structure should follow headcount and risk profile. Work out which parts of the CIA triad your threat profile actually stresses, staff for that, and choose an org model deliberately rather than inheriting one.
beliefs.src: How to Structure Security for a Big Org.txt

beliefs.title: FDEs are an access question
beliefs.body: Forward deployed engineers exist because the bottleneck moved from model capability to deployment reality. For anyone in security this matters twice: FDEs get deep access to production systems by design, and what they leave behind becomes part of the attack surface someone has to defend.
beliefs.src: What is a Forward Deployed Engineer.txt

writing.title: AI Security vs. Traditional Cybersecurity
writing.summary: Argues the two fields overlap rather than one containing the other, and explains why AI-specific risks still deserve separate attention. Short, opinionated, publishable as-is.

writing.title: How to Structure Security for a Big Organization
writing.summary: Lays out the functions every security org needs and the five structural models, then argues most orgs drift into a shape built by history rather than chosen on purpose. Well-sourced with external citations.

writing.title: What is a Forward Deployed Engineer

writing.src: What is a Forward Deployed Engineer.txt

writing.title: Supply Chain and Dependency Compromises
writing.summary: Walks through every stage of an AI system, from training notebook to production jump host, mapping where supply chain compromise can enter. Detailed and technical.

writing.title: Data Attacks
writing.summary: Explains how training data poisoning and feature manipulation compromise a model before it ever reaches production, mapped to MITRE ATLAS stages. Technically precise.
writing.why_not: Written as a chapter section referencing an unincluded system diagram; needs rewriting to stand alone.

voice_notes: She writes in short, direct sentences and states her own position plainly, often opening with 'I see' or 'I think' rather than hedging. She favours concrete, sometimes blunt framing ("the reason is blunt") over abstraction, and reaches for one clear metaphor per piece (a Venn diagram, a shape built by history) rather than stacking imagery. Technical pieces are structured and list-driven, mapping ideas to named frameworks like MITRE ATLAS. She rarely uses humour; the tone is measured and explanatory, closer to a briefing than a blog post. She cites sources plainly at the end of longer pieces rather than working links into the prose.

quotes.text: I see AI security and cybersecurity as overlapping fields, much like a Venn diagram.
The structure ends up reflecting yesterday's dynamics rather than today's operating reality: a shape built by history instead of chosen on purpose.

quotes.text: The reason is blunt: the hard part of AI is not the model.
